text.p: The following are the main stories from Tuesday morning's Austrian newspapers:
- Austria goes off-line for two hours today as domestic internet providers vent their anger at a police raid on one of their Viennese counterparts.
- Austria's science establishment is up in arms over the government's plans to slice eight percent off funds earmarked for research.
- Social Democrat Siegbert Metelko, who suffered a crushing defeat to the conservative People's Party candidate in the Klagenfurt mayoral elections, has hinted he may step down.
- People's Party urges for speedy return of Bosnian refugees to their homeland.
- Austrian Airlines' director of the board, Mario Rehulka, said "together with Lauda Air we will be very much on the offensive in the international arena."
- Creditansalt sells its entire stake in machine maker Andritz to Germany's AGIV AG. AGIV now holds 93 percent of Andritz.
- Porcelain maker Augarten says it will swing into the black in 2001.
- It would be very risky and expensive if Austria chooses to go it alone on road pricing, international consultancy Arthur D. Little warned.

- Bank Austria chief executive Gerhard Randa and the head of Austrian state holding company OeIAG, Karl Hollweger, must present an exact privatisation concept by the end of April for the government's 19 percent stake in Bank Austria, said Finance Minister Rudolf Edlinger.
- Bank Austria holds 10 percent of EA-Generali.
- Austria will participate in a protection force for Albania. Military assistance would only be used for the safeguarding of aid deliveries, Foreign Minister Wolfgang Schuessel said.
